title: Starter Spark SDK accelerator — quickstart & sprint notes
content:
Context:
This doc captures a compact, opinionated playbook for a 2-week accelerator sprint (Starter Spark) to produce: a zero-friction quickstart, a tiny sample app, a local-mode emulator, and an observability/telemetry baseline so a new engineer can go from signup -> instrumented sample in ~15 minutes.

Why this exists (problem):
- Current quickstarts are too many variants; friction points: API keys, default timeouts, local network quirks.
- Engineers drop off before seeing telemetry or understanding cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Need a battery-included tiny app that demonstrates caching, batching, and graceful fallback.

Sprint goals (MVP):
- Deliver a single opinionated quickstart page + 3-language sample app (JS, Python, Go).
- Build rw-spark CLI that scaffolds app + local emulator (hermetic).
- Ship minimal telemetry contract and a dashboard sample.
- Create 5 micro-lessons: "first call", "handle 429s", "measure tokens & cost", "local-mode debugging", "rollout to Dedicated".

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Fresh account: follow README -> run 'rw-spark start' -> see streaming response in terminal within 15 minutes.
- Emulator supports stubbing responses and simulating latency (50ms/200ms/1s).
- Telemetry events emitted for: request_start, request_end, token_count, fallback_triggered.
- One e2e test that runs the sample app against emulator in CI.

Quickstart sketch (user flow):
1) Sign up and get an API key (free credits) — single link in quickstart page.
2) git clone starter-spark-template && cd starter-spark-template
3) rw-spark init --lang js --sample=todo
   - rw-spark will create: package.json, sample app, .env.example, local-emulator config
4) cp .env.example .env && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_test_xxx
5) rw-spark start (starts local emu + dev server)
6) Open http://localhost:3000 and run the sample prompt. Observe streaming in UI + metrics printed in terminal.

CLI behavior & ergonomics notes (rw-spark):
- Defaults to smallest sample set (minimal dependencies).
- Interactive prompts for network proxy (detect common corp proxies).
- Built-in command: 'rw-spark smoke' runs 3 sanity calls, prints latency p50/p95 and token usage.
- 'rw-spark inject-failures --type=latency --ms=1000' used by debugging labs.

Local emulator (requirements):
- Language-agnostic HTTP shim that mimics Redwood hosted API surface: /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings
- Options: deterministic stubs based on prompt fingerprint; scripted delays; ability to swap in a tiny local model for realism (opt-in).
- Runs as single binary (Go) or docker image.

Telemetry contract (minimal):
- Events (names and minimal schema):
  - request_start: {session_id, route, model_hint, request_id, sample_app}
  - request_end: {request_id, status, latency_ms, bytes_sent, bytes_received}
  - token_count: {request_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}
  - fallback_triggered: {request_id, fallback_reason, fallback_model}
- Transport: client emits to console + file in local-mode. In hosted quickstart we send to a sandbox telemetry endpoint (no PII).
- Sampling: 100% in quickstart; SDKs default to 0.1% in production.

Sample app outline (todo-list assistant):
- UI: minimal web app (single page) with text area for prompt, buttons for streaming/complete, indicator for token estimate and estimated cost.
- Patterns showcased: streaming handler, retries with jitter, cache-first optimistic rendering, simple reranking of multiple outputs.
- Tests: unit for retry backoff logic, integration test against emulator verifying fallback behavior.

Developer-facing docs structure (on quickstart page):
- Top: 3-step TL;DR with explicit timing ("15 minutes").
- Troubleshooting section: common errors, corporate proxy notes, token mismatch.
- Sections: Quickstart, Local debugging, Observability, When to go Dedicated, Glossary (tokens, KV cache, quantization).

Observability sample dashboard (what to show):
- Live stream of request_start/request_end, p50/p95 latency by route, token usage histogram, fallback rate.
- Cost estimate panel (simulated cost for sample workload).

Performance guardrails to teach (in labs):
- When to batch vs stream: heuristics and simple decision tree.
- Default per-request timeout: 8s in quickstart; show lowering to 1.5s for strict UI.
- Recommended retry policy: max 2 retries, exponential backoff starting at 200ms + jitter.

Rollout plan for the starter kit:
- Week 0: prototype CLI + JS sample + emulator + docs sketch (this sprint).
- Week 1: add Python + Go samples, telemetry + CI smoke tests.
- Week 2: internal dogfood (select teams try kit), iterate based on feedback, finalize quickstart page and embed in Console onboarding.

Risk log & mitigations: 
- Risk: Emulator diverges from hosted API behavior -> mitigation: include a compatibility test that runs against a real hosted sandbox each week.
- Risk: Too opinionated defaults alienate advanced users -> mitigation: include an "advanced mode" toggle and explictly document what defaults do.
- Risk: Telemetry leaks secrets -> mitigation: scrub API keys and PII client-side; telemetry endpoint is sandboxed.

Open questions (to resolve during sprint):
- Should the emulator include a local tiny LM (optional) or always stub responses? (tradeoffs: size vs realism)
- What is the minimum set of sample prompts that convincingly show caching and batching?
- Do we implement per-token cost estimation client-side or fetch price table from server?

Notes to self / sprint reminders: 
- Keep samples <100 LOC for each language.
- Prioritize reproducible CI e2e for emulator.
- Add a "playback" feature to telemetry so demo owners can replay a user session.
- Coordinate with Console team to include a one-click "open this sample in sandbox" link.

Mini-checklist for first PR: 
- [ ] rw-spark CLI scaffold + README
- [ ] JS sample app + package.json
- [ ] Local emulator binary + dockerfile
- [ ] Telemetry shim + example dashboard JSON
- [ ] CI e2e that runs emulator smoke tests

User stories (short):
- As a new developer, I want a one-command scaffold so I can see a streaming chat demo in under 15 minutes.
- As an engineer on mobile team, I want a small Python example showing tokens & cost so I can estimate budget for a POC.
- As a product manager, I want to see fallback rates in a dashboard while we test an A/B rollout.

Appendix: example terminal transcript (simulated)
$ git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/starter-spark-template.git
$ cd starter-spark-template && rw-spark init --lang js
created: package.json
created: src/index.js
created: .env.example
$ cp .env.example .env && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_test_123
$ rw-spark start
[emulator] listening on http://localhost:8312
[devserver] started on http://localhost:3000
[smoke] request_start req=abc123 route=/v1/chat
[smoke] request_end req=abc123 status=200 latency_ms=142 tokens=78
Open browser -> hit "Create todo" -> streaming response begins (first tokens within 120ms)

End of draft — notes: keep this doc lightweight and iteratively refine after first dogfood run.
